title: "Set up the course MCP servers and the course LLM gateway"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2
---

This page sets up your coding assistant for the course: it connects the assistant to the course MCP server `436c`
and to the AWS Knowledge MCP server `aws-knowledge`, and it gives your own code the address and key of the course
LLM gateway. The settings go in your user configuration on your laptop, so they work in every folder and the token
never lands in a repository.

**For you, the student.** Start your assistant in a terminal and give it this user message:

```text
Run curl -sL https://ilm.wiki/436c/setup
and follow the page it prints to set me up.
```

The assistant asks you to set your token, writes its configuration, asks you to restart it, and then runs the
checks. Your token is in the issue "Your course MCP tokens" in your team repository, next to your name. You set it
yourself in a terminal; you do not paste it into the chat.

The rest of this page is written for the assistant.

## Rules for the assistant

1. Never ask the student to paste the token into this chat, and never print it. Check only that it is set.
2. Never write the token into an assistant's configuration file or into a repository. Every configuration below
   reads it from the environment variable `KB_MCP_TOKEN`, which the student sets in Step 2.
3. Write user-level configuration, in the student's home folder. Never write a configuration file inside a git
   repository.
4. Add to an existing configuration file: keep every server and setting already in it. If the file has a server
   named `436c` or `aws-knowledge` with other values, show the student both versions and ask before replacing it.
5. Do the steps in order and tell the student what each command does before running it.

## Values

| Value | Setting |
|---|---|
| Course MCP server `436c` | `https://kb-cloud-students.fly.dev/mcp`, header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| AWS Knowledge MCP server `aws-knowledge` | `https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws`, no token |
| Course LLM gateway, base URL | `https://oay6tcpsuv4gn5mubtlj7rnbl40gmrlv.lambda-url.ca-central-1.on.aws/v1` |
| Token | environment variable `KB_MCP_TOKEN`; the same token is the API key for the course LLM gateway |

## Step 1: find out which assistant you are

Find out which assistant and operating system the student uses: Claude Code, Kiro IDE, Kiro CLI, Codex, or GitHub
Copilot (in VS Code or the Copilot CLI); macOS, Linux or Windows. If you are not sure, ask the student.

## Step 2: the student sets the token

Ask the student to copy their token from the issue "Your course MCP tokens" in their team repository and to make
the setting permanent, so that an assistant started from an app icon also sees it. Give the student the commands
for their system and ask them to run them in their own terminal, replacing `paste-your-token-here` and keeping the
quotes.

macOS (zsh):

```bash
echo "export KB_MCP_TOKEN='paste-your-token-here'" \
  >> ~/.zshrc
```

Linux (bash):

```bash
echo "export KB_MCP_TOKEN='paste-your-token-here'" \
  >> ~/.bashrc
```

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
setx KB_MCP_TOKEN "paste-your-token-here"
```

The setting applies to terminals and apps opened after it. Ask the student to open a new terminal and run the check
for their system, which prints `set` without printing the token:

```bash
test -n "$KB_MCP_TOKEN" && echo set
```

```powershell
if ($env:KB_MCP_TOKEN) { "set" }
```

## Step 3: write the configuration for your assistant

Write only the section for the student's assistant. On Windows, `~` is the user's home folder, `%USERPROFILE%`.

### Claude Code

Run these two commands. Keep the single quotes around the header: they make Claude Code store the text
`${KB_MCP_TOKEN}` and read the token when it starts, instead of storing the token itself.

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user \
  436c https://kb-cloud-students.fly.dev/mcp \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer ${KB_MCP_TOKEN}'
```

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user \
  aws-knowledge https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws
```

In PowerShell, run each command on one line, with the same single quotes. Both servers go into `~/.claude.json`,
for all the student's folders ([Claude Code MCP](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp)). If the team repository
already has a `.mcp.json` copied from `.mcp.json.example`, it can stay: it names the same two servers with the same
settings.

### Kiro IDE and Kiro CLI

Both read `~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json`
([Kiro MCP configuration](https://kiro.dev/docs/mcp/configuration/#configuration-locations)). Add these two
servers under `mcpServers`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "436c": {
      "url": "https://kb-cloud-students.fly.dev/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${KB_MCP_TOKEN}"
      }
    },
    "aws-knowledge": {
      "url": "https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws"
    }
  }
}
```

In the Kiro IDE, the student also adds `KB_MCP_TOKEN` to the approved variables: open Settings, search for
**Mcp Approved Env Vars** and add `KB_MCP_TOKEN`. Kiro expands only approved variables
([Kiro environment variables](https://kiro.dev/docs/mcp/configuration/#environment-variables)).

### Codex

Add these tables to `~/.codex/config.toml`
([Codex MCP](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli)):

```toml
[mcp_servers.436c]
url = "https://kb-cloud-students.fly.dev/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "KB_MCP_TOKEN"

[mcp_servers.aws-knowledge]
url = "https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws"
```

### GitHub Copilot (VS Code or Copilot CLI)

Add these two servers under `mcpServers` in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`
([VS Code MCP configuration](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/mcp-configuration)):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "436c": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://kb-cloud-students.fly.dev/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${KB_MCP_TOKEN}"
      },
      "tools": ["*"]
    },
    "aws-knowledge": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws",
      "tools": ["*"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Step 4: set the course LLM gateway for the student's code

Do this step for every assistant. Course code and Inspect read the gateway from these variables. Give the student
the lines for their system to run in their own terminal:

macOS (zsh; on Linux, use `~/.bashrc`):

```bash
cat >> ~/.zshrc <<'EOF'
export COURSE_GATEWAY_URL=https://oay6tcpsuv4gn5mubtlj7rnbl40gmrlv.lambda-url.ca-central-1.on.aws/v1
export PROXY_BASE_URL=$COURSE_GATEWAY_URL
export PROXY_API_KEY=$KB_MCP_TOKEN
EOF
```

Windows PowerShell, after the token is set and in a new terminal:

```powershell
setx COURSE_GATEWAY_URL "https://oay6tcpsuv4gn5mubtlj7rnbl40gmrlv.lambda-url.ca-central-1.on.aws/v1"
setx PROXY_BASE_URL "https://oay6tcpsuv4gn5mubtlj7rnbl40gmrlv.lambda-url.ca-central-1.on.aws/v1"
setx PROXY_API_KEY "$env:KB_MCP_TOKEN"
```

Do not set `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_BASE_URL` for the whole user account: other tools on the laptop read them.
Set them only in the project's own code or its untracked `.env` file.

## Step 5: the student restarts the assistant

An assistant reads its MCP configuration and the environment when it starts. Ask the student to:

1. Quit the assistant fully.
2. Open a new terminal, or reopen the app, so it reads the token setting.
3. Start the assistant again: `claude`, `kiro-cli chat` or `codex` in the new terminal, or open the Kiro IDE or
   VS Code.
4. Give it this user message:

   ```text
   Run curl -sL https://ilm.wiki/436c/setup
   and do Step 6 of the page it prints.
   ```

## Step 6: check both servers and the gateway

1. **Course MCP server.** Call the `cpsc436c_start_here` tool of the server `436c` and show the student the tool
   result. Then list the tools of `436c`. The list includes `cpsc436c_search`, `cpsc436c_read`, `cpsc436c_list`
   and `cpsc436c_start_here`; the older names `query_kb`, `get_kb_doc` and `list_kb_topics` do the same.
2. **AWS Knowledge MCP server.** List the tools of `aws-knowledge`. The list includes a documentation search tool.
3. **Where the student sees the connection:**

   | Assistant | Where |
   |---|---|
   | Claude Code | `claude mcp list` in a terminal shows `436c` and `aws-knowledge` as `✔ Connected`; `/mcp` in the chat shows their tools |
   | Kiro IDE | Kiro panel (Kiro icon on the left bar), section **MCP Servers** |
   | Kiro CLI | `/mcp` in a `kiro-cli chat` session; `kiro-cli mcp list` shows only the servers in the files, not whether they connect |
   | Codex | `/mcp` in the `codex` chat; `codex mcp list` in a terminal |
   | Copilot | VS Code: command **Chat: Open Customizations**, then **MCP Servers** |

4. **Course LLM gateway.** Run the command for the student's system. It asks for the list of models and does not
   call a model.

   ```bash
   curl -s \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $KB_MCP_TOKEN" \
     https://oay6tcpsuv4gn5mubtlj7rnbl40gmrlv.lambda-url.ca-central-1.on.aws/v1/models
   ```

   ```powershell
   curl.exe -s `
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $env:KB_MCP_TOKEN" `
     https://oay6tcpsuv4gn5mubtlj7rnbl40gmrlv.lambda-url.ca-central-1.on.aws/v1/models
   ```

   The reply lists `qwen3.8-27b`, `qwen3.6-35b-a3b` and `qwen3-embedding-0.6b`.

Tell the student which checks passed. If all passed, the setup is done.

## If a check fails

| What you see | What to do |
|---|---|
| `436c` failed with `HTTP 401` or `invalid_token`; the gateway replies `missing or malformed API key` | The token did not reach the assistant, or it is not the student's current token. Ask the student to copy the token again from "Your course MCP tokens" and to set it again as in Step 2: in `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`, replace the old `export KB_MCP_TOKEN` line in their editor; on Windows, run `setx KB_MCP_TOKEN` and `setx PROXY_API_KEY` again with the new token. Then repeat Step 5. The server's message about clearing authentication and re-registering does not apply: the course server uses this token only |
| Claude Code warns `Missing environment variables: KB_MCP_TOKEN` | The assistant was started before the token was set. Repeat Step 5 |
| Kiro warns that `KB_MCP_TOKEN` is not approved | Add it under **Mcp Approved Env Vars** (Step 3, Kiro), then restart Kiro |
| Kiro CLI: `/mcp` lists neither server, but `kiro-cli mcp list` shows them | The agent in the chat may not include the MCP files. In its agent configuration, `includeMcpJson` must be `true` ([Kiro agent configuration](https://kiro.dev/docs/custom-agents/configuration-reference/)). Ask a TA if it is |
| `aws-knowledge` fails as well | The laptop cannot reach the internet from the assistant. Try without the VPN, or ask a TA about the network |
| `could not resolve host` for `ilm.wiki` | Use the page's address instead: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cpsc436c-2026w1/lecture-reviews/main/assistant-setup.qmd` |

If a fix does not work, stop and ask the student to show the output to a TA. Do not put the token into a
configuration file to make a check pass.
